title: Naval Topic 10 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: To act in a way that matches a promise, belief, standard, or expectation.
exs: The new salon didn't live up to the reviews.
I try to live up to my own rules.

src.t: I asked him why, and he said, “I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.”
src.zh: 我问他为什么，他说：“我开始觉得，既然我在公开场合说了那些话，那私底下也应该真正做到。”

lg: 踮起脚够到那条标准线。

cards.ex: Away from other people, where a conversation or action is not public.
exs: Can we talk in private?
She practices English in private before class.

src.t: I asked him why, and he said, “I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.”
src.zh: 我问他为什么，他说：“我开始觉得，既然我在公开场合说了那些话，那私底下也应该真正做到。”

lg: 关上门，没人看见的时候。

cards.ex: Where other people can see or hear you.
exs: He never complains in public.
I get nervous speaking English in public.

src.t: I asked him why, and he said, “I started feeling like I had to live up to in private the things that I was saying in public.”
src.zh: 我问他为什么，他说：“我开始觉得，既然我在公开场合说了那些话，那私底下也应该真正做到。”

lg: 站在大家都看得见的地方。

cards.ex: Showing poor judgment, especially when you should know better.
exs: It was foolish to book ten clients in one day.
Don't feel foolish for asking questions.

src.t: It’s what Emerson said, “Foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.”
src.zh: 就像爱默生说的：“愚蠢地坚持前后一致，是思想狭隘之人的心魔。”

cards.ex: Staying the same over time, or making your actions match your words.
exs: Consistency builds trust with clients.
Foolish consistency means never changing even when you're wrong.

src.t: It’s what Emerson said, “Foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.”
src.zh: 就像爱默生说的：“愚蠢地坚持前后一致，是思想狭隘之人的心魔。”

lg: 每天放一块砖，一直不断。
cards.note: “一致性”不等于机械重复同一个动作；是不同时间里行为/说法保持稳定，或言行相符。文中 foolish consistency 指拒绝更新观点。

cards.ex: A small creature in old stories; here, a fear or idea that controls how someone thinks.
exs: Fear is the hobgoblin that stops me from trying.
In the story, a hobgoblin hid in the kitchen.

src.t: It’s what Emerson said, “Foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds.”
src.zh: 就像爱默生说的：“愚蠢地坚持前后一致，是思想狭隘之人的心魔。”

lg: 藏在角落里捣乱的小妖怪。

cards.ex: Looking at the main point rather than the less important details.
exs: Essentially, a refill is a small touch-up.
The two glues are essentially the same.

src.t: But essentially, look, all learning is error correction.
src.zh: 但本质上，你看，所有的学习都是纠错。

cards.ex: Finding what is wrong and changing it to make it right.
exs: Learning a language is mostly error correction.
My teacher does error correction after I speak.

src.t: But essentially, look, all learning is error correction.
src.zh: 但本质上，你看，所有的学习都是纠错。

lg: 发现写错的地方，划掉改对。

cards.ex: What you know or understand from learning and experience.
exs: Her knowledge of lash styles is amazing.
Knowledge grows when you share it.

src.t: Every knowledge creation system works through making guesses and correcting errors.
src.zh: 每一个创造知识的系统，都是靠猜测和纠正错误来运作的。

cards.ex: An answer or opinion you give when you are not sure.
exs: My best guess is that she'll be late.
Make a guess, then check.

src.t: Every knowledge creation system works through making guesses and correcting errors.
src.zh: 每一个创造知识的系统，都是靠猜测和纠正错误来运作的。

cards.ex: Because of what the word or idea itself means.
exs: A beginner, by definition, makes mistakes.
A secret, by definition, isn't shared.

src.t: So by definition, if you’re learning, you’re going to be wrong most of the time and you’ll be updating your priors.
src.zh: 所以，从学习本身的定义来看，只要你还在学习，就难免经常判断错，也会不断根据新信息修正原先的判断。

lg: 字典上写的意思就决定了。

cards.ex: Beliefs or expectations you already have before seeing new evidence.
exs: New facts should update your priors.
Check your priors before you judge.

src.t: So by definition, if you’re learning, you’re going to be wrong most of the time and you’ll be updating your priors.
src.zh: 所以，从学习本身的定义来看，只要你还在学习，就难免经常判断错，也会不断根据新信息修正原先的判断。

lg: 看到新证据之前，心里已有的判断。
cards.note: 这是带概率/判断色彩的“先前信念”；看到新证据后更新，不只是改变喜好。

cards.ex: To point out something someone said or did, often because you think it is wrong.
exs: She called him out for being rude.
People love to call out celebrities online.

src.t: For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.
src.zh: 比如，我大概八九年前参加过一期 Joe Rogan 的播客，后来人们就会专门挑出其中那一件最终被证明不正确的事来说。

lg: 大声把别人的错指出来。

cards.ex: To become clear or be discovered as the final result.
exs: The new style turned out great.
It turned out she was right.

src.t: For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.
src.zh: 比如，我大概八九年前参加过一期 Joe Rogan 的播客，后来人们就会专门挑出其中那一件最终被证明不正确的事来说。

cards.note: turn out to be + adjective/noun = 随着事实发展，最终发现/证明是……；didn’t turn out to be correct 否定的是最终结果。

cards.ex: To keep criticizing or attacking someone or something.
exs: Stop beating on yourself for one mistake.
The comments kept beating on his old video.

src.t: They just beat on it because it helps them in their mind raise their status a little bit – “I caught him in an error.”
src.zh: 他们就揪着不放，因为在他们心里这能让自己的地位提高一点——“我抓到他犯错了。”

cards.ex: To discover someone doing something wrong, often while they are doing it.
exs: I caught him in a lie.
She caught me in a small error.

src.t: They just beat on it because it helps them in their mind raise their status a little bit – “I caught him in an error.”
src.zh: 他们就揪着不放，因为在他们心里这能让自己的地位提高一点——“我抓到他犯错了。”

cards.ex: Very obvious and bad, without any attempt to hide it.
exs: That's a blatant lie.
It was a blatant copy of my design.

src.t: If you catch someone in a blatant lie where they believe one thing and say another, that’s legit – that’s a character flaw.
src.zh: 如果你抓到某人公然撒谎，心里信一套、嘴上说一套，那批评是合理的——那是人品缺陷。

cards.ex: Real, acceptable, or reasonable; an informal way to say something is valid.
exs: Is this offer legit?
Her complaint is totally legit.

src.t: If you catch someone in a blatant lie where they believe one thing and say another, that’s legit – that’s a character flaw.
src.zh: 如果你抓到某人公然撒谎，心里信一套、嘴上说一套，那批评是合理的——那是人品缺陷。

cards.note: 此处 “that’s legit” = 那样指出对方撒谎是有道理的；不是指谎言本身是真的。

cards.ex: A weakness in the way someone behaves or treats other people.
exs: Being late all the time is a character flaw.
Lying is a serious character flaw.

src.t: If you catch someone in a blatant lie where they believe one thing and say another, that’s legit – that’s a character flaw.
src.zh: 如果你抓到某人公然撒谎，心里信一套、嘴上说一套，那批评是合理的——那是人品缺陷。

lg: 性格这块拼图上的一道裂缝。

cards.ex: Saying something you know is not true, usually to make someone believe it.
exs: Lying to clients ruins trust.
He's not good at lying.

src.t: They shouldn’t be lying.
src.zh: 他们不该撒谎。

cards.note: 在 They shouldn’t be lying 中 lying 是 lie 的 -ing 动词形式，不应标作普通名词；名词用法需另举例。

cards.ex: Used to introduce a different side of a situation or argument.
exs: Classic lashes are quick. On the other hand, volume looks fuller.
On the other hand, it's expensive.

src.t: But on the other hand, if they just made a guess at something and they got it wrong.
src.zh: 但另一方面，如果他们只是对某件事做了猜测，结果猜错了。

lg: 左手拿一个观点，再换到另一只手看反面

cards.ex: To make a mistake about a fact, answer, or situation.
exs: I got the date wrong.
It's okay to get it wrong sometimes.

src.t: But on the other hand, if they just made a guess at something and they got it wrong.
src.zh: 但另一方面，如果他们只是对某件事做了猜测，结果猜错了。

cards.ex: A situation that is different from the one you were just discussing.
exs: Classic sets are easy. Mega volume is a different story.
Talking is easy; doing it is a different story.

src.t: Mostly it’s about the AI AGI thing, and I think I’m still right about that, but it’s a different story.
src.zh: 主要是关于 AI、AGI 那件事，我觉得我在这点上还是对的，不过那是另一回事了。

cards.ex: To successfully reach a goal, often through effort.
exs: She achieved her goal of opening a studio.
You can achieve a lot in a year.

src.t: People who think we have achieved AGI just fail a Turing test from their side.
src.zh: 那些觉得我们已经实现 AGI 的人，在我看来反倒是他们自己没通过图灵测试。

lg: 努力之后，终于够到目标

cards.ex: A test of whether a machine can communicate in a way people mistake for a human.
exs: Some chatbots can almost pass the Turing test.
We talked about the Turing test in class.

src.t: People who think we have achieved AGI just fail a Turing test from their side.
src.zh: 那些觉得我们已经实现 AGI 的人，在我看来反倒是他们自己没通过图灵测试。

lg: 隔着屏幕，分不出是人还是机器。

cards.ex: To become strongly interested in an idea or detail and keep focusing on it.
exs: The media latched onto one word he said.
Kids latch onto new words fast.

src.t: It’s funny how people latch onto single proclamations, but the reality is all of us are dynamical systems.
src.zh: 有意思的是，人们会死抓住某一句表态不放，但现实是，我们每个人都是不断变化的动态系统。

lg: 像钩子一样挂住就不松。

cards.ex: Systems whose state changes over time as different parts affect one another.
exs: Weather is a dynamical system.
We are dynamical systems, always changing.

src.t: It’s funny how people latch onto single proclamations, but the reality is all of us are dynamical systems.
src.zh: 有意思的是，人们会死抓住某一句表态不放，但现实是，我们每个人都是不断变化的动态系统。

lg: 一直在流动、变化的整体。

cards.ex: To develop, improve, or become bigger over time.
exs: My business grew a lot this year.
You grow when you leave your comfort zone.

src.t: We’re always changing, always learning, always growing, and hopefully we’re correcting errors.
src.zh: 我们一直在变、一直在学、一直在成长，希望也一直在纠正错误。

cards.ex: To seem attractive or successful to other people.
exs: He only wants to look good online.
These lashes make you look good in photos.

src.t: But what you don’t want to be doing is lying in public because you’re trying to look good.
src.zh: 但你不该做的，是为了让自己显得好而在公开场合撒谎。

cards.ex: To notice something with your nose; informally, to sense something without being told.
exs: I can smell a fake review.
Kids can smell when you're nervous.

src.t: I think people can smell that.
src.zh: 我觉得大家其实能察觉出来。

lg: 鼻子一闻就知道不对劲。

cards.ex: To not have enough of something you need or expect.
exs: This room lacks light.
She doesn't lack confidence.

src.t: What this world really lacks right now is authenticity, because everybody wants something.
src.zh: 现在这个世界真正缺少的是真诚，因为每个人都想要点什么。

cards.ex: Being real and honest about who you are and what you believe, instead of pretending.
exs: Clients love her authenticity.
Authenticity is rare online.

src.t: What this world really lacks right now is authenticity, because everybody wants something.
src.zh: 现在这个世界真正缺少的是真诚，因为每个人都想要点什么。

cards.note: 不只是“真货”；这里是言行、内心信念与对外形象一致，不为取悦别人扮演另一个自己。

cards.ex: To be thought of or judged in a particular way by other people.
exs: She wants to be seen as an expert.
He's seen as a leader.

src.t: They want to be seen as something, they want to be something that they’re not.
src.zh: 他们想被看作某种人，想成为自己本来不是的样子。

lg: 别人眼里给你贴的标签。

cards.ex: Quick to notice or react to small changes, feelings, or situations.
exs: My eyes are sensitive to glue fumes.
Kids are very sensitive to tone.

src.t: So you catch a lot of people saying things that they don’t really believe, and I think people are very sensitive to that.
src.zh: 所以你会发现很多人说着自己并不真信的话，我觉得大家对此非常敏感。

lg: 一点点变化都能感觉到。

cards.ex: A system that detects things; informally, your ability to notice signs of something.
exs: My lie radar went off.
She has a great radar for good clients.

src.t: Bullshit radars have become hypersensitized to try and work out whether or not this person means the thing that they’re saying.
src.zh: 人们识别虚假和不真诚言论的“雷达”已经变得异常敏感，总想弄清楚一个人说的话到底是不是真心的。

lg: 远远就能探测到的感应器。

cards.ex: Made unusually sensitive, so even small signs can cause a strong reaction.
exs: People are hypersensitized to ads now.
After the scam, I'm hypersensitized to strange emails.

src.t: Bullshit radars have become hypersensitized to try and work out whether or not this person means the thing that they’re saying.
src.zh: 人们识别虚假和不真诚言论的“雷达”已经变得异常敏感，总想弄清楚一个人说的话到底是不是真心的。

cards.note: hyper-（过度）+ sensit-（敏感）+ -ized（变得/被使得）；与 hypo-（不足）和 dehydrated（脱水，de-）区分。

cards.ex: To understand something after thinking about it or looking at the facts.
exs: I can't work out what she wants.
We'll work out a plan.

src.t: Bullshit radars have become hypersensitized to try and work out whether or not this person means the thing that they’re saying.
src.zh: 人们识别虚假和不真诚言论的“雷达”已经变得异常敏感，总想弄清楚一个人说的话到底是不是真心的。

cards.note: 在本段是“通过思考弄清楚”，不是健身，也不是事情进展顺利。

cards.ex: A serious attempt to do something, especially something new or difficult.
exs: Opening a studio was a big endeavor.
Good luck in your new endeavor.

src.t: Most of us are wrong most of the time, especially in any new endeavor.
src.zh: 我们大多数人大部分时候都是错的，尤其是在做任何新尝试的时候。

cards.ex: Used to add a contrast or make a point less absolute, often at the end of a sentence.
exs: It's expensive. It's worth it, though.
Nice day. A bit cold, though.

src.t: There’s a difference between being wrong and disingenuous though.
src.zh: 不过，说错了和明知不真诚却故意那样说，是两回事。

cards.ex: Right or accurate; as a response, it means “Yes, that is right.”
exs: Is this the correct address?
That's correct.

src.t: Correct.
src.zh: 没错。

cards.ex: Done on purpose rather than by accident.
exs: He purposefully ignored my message.
I purposefully booked a quiet day.

src.t: Purposefully wrong.
src.zh: 故意说错。

exzh: 我特意约了一个清闲的日子。

cards.ex: Used when something matches what was said or expected, without any difference.
exs: Exactly! That's what I meant.
It costs exactly fifty dollars.

src.t: Exactly.
src.zh: 正是。

cards.ex: Not a serious problem; nothing to worry much about.
exs: You're five minutes late? No big deal.
Forgetting once is no big deal.

src.t: If someone is wrong, no big deal, as long as they have a genuine reason for saying what they’re saying or believing what they’re believing.
src.zh: 一个人说错了也没什么大不了，只要他确实有真诚的理由，才会说那些话、相信那些事。

cards.ex: Only if a particular condition is true or continues to be true.
exs: You can book any time, as long as you call first.
It's fine as long as you're happy.

src.t: If someone is wrong, no big deal, as long as they have a genuine reason for saying what they’re saying or believing what they’re believing.
src.zh: 一个人说错了也没什么大不了，只要他确实有真诚的理由，才会说那些话、相信那些事。

cards.ex: Real and sincere, not fake or pretending.
exs: She has a genuine smile.
Is this genuine leather?

src.t: If someone is wrong, no big deal, as long as they have a genuine reason for saying what they’re saying or believing what they’re believing.
src.zh: 一个人说错了也没什么大不了，只要他确实有真诚的理由，才会说那些话、相信那些事。

lg: 内心真实想法与说出来的东西一致；不伪装、不作假。
cards.note: genuine ≠ 必然正确；是真实、真诚而非故意装出来。

cards.ex: To raise something to a higher level, position, or status.
exs: Good lighting can elevate your photos.
He lied to elevate his status.

src.t: But if they are lying to elevate their status or their appearance or to live up to some expectation, that’s the mistake.
src.zh: 但如果他们撒谎是为了抬高自己的地位、形象，或者为了符合某种期待，那就错了。

cards.ex: How someone or something looks, or the impression they give other people.
exs: She cares a lot about her appearance.
Don't judge by appearance.

src.t: But if they are lying to elevate their status or their appearance or to live up to some expectation, that’s the mistake.
src.zh: 但如果他们撒谎是为了抬高自己的地位、形象，或者为了符合某种期待，那就错了。

cards.ex: A belief about what will probably happen or what someone should do.
exs: The results were beyond my expectations.
Clients have high expectations.

src.t: But if they are lying to elevate their status or their appearance or to live up to some expectation, that’s the mistake.
src.zh: 但如果他们撒谎是为了抬高自己的地位、形象，或者为了符合某种期待，那就错了。

cards.ex: A person who listens to someone speaking.
exs: He's a good listener.
The podcast has many listeners.

src.t: And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.
src.zh: 而且这不只是误导听众，对说话的人自己也有害，因为他最后会困在一个真假难辨、不断自我欺骗的“镜子迷宫”里。

cards.zh: 镜子迷宫（真假难辨的处境）
cards.ex: A confusing situation in which appearances and repeated false stories hide what is real.
exs: Lying puts you in a hall of mirrors.
Social media can feel like a hall of mirrors.

src.t: And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.
src.zh: 而且这不只是误导听众，对说话的人自己也有害，因为他最后会困在一个真假难辨、不断自我欺骗的“镜子迷宫”里。

lg: 四面都是镜子，找不到真自己。

cards.ex: Making yourself believe something that you know, or suspect, is not true.
exs: Stop lying to yourself; you need rest.
If you lie to others, you'll end up lying to yourself.

src.t: You yourself are going to be consistent with your past proclamations, so if you’re lying to others, you’re going to be lying to yourself.
src.zh: 你自己会努力和过去的表态保持一致，所以如果你对别人撒谎，你也会对自己撒谎。

cards.ex: Controlled like a puppet, instead of making your own choices.
exs: He felt puppeted by his fans.
Don't be puppeted by other people's opinions.

src.t: You’re puppeted by a person that you are not even.
src.zh: 你就像被一个根本不是真实自己的虚构形象牵着走。

lg: 身上绑着线，别人一拉就动。
cards.note: 在 You’re puppeted ... 中为过去分词构成被动/状态化用法；仅标 adjective 不够准确。

cards.ex: A sentence from a speech, film, book, or conversation.
exs: What's that famous line from the movie?
I love that line.

src.t: It’s like, what was the line?
src.zh: 就像，那句话是怎么说的来着？

cards.ex: Used to explain the main idea in simple terms.
exs: Basically, I need more sleep.
It's basically the same style.

src.t: You’re basically trying to impress people who don’t care about you.
src.zh: 说白了，你一直在努力让那些根本不在乎你的人对你刮目相看。

cards.ex: To make someone admire you or think highly of you.
exs: She wanted to impress her new boss.
Don't try to impress everyone.

src.t: You’re basically trying to impress people who don’t care about you.
src.zh: 说白了，你一直在努力让那些根本不在乎你的人对你刮目相看。

cards.note: “让别人佩服/留下印象”是核心；“讨好”是上下文可能产生的效果，不是词本身的基本义。

cards.ex: To feel that someone or something matters to you.
exs: I care about my clients.
He doesn't care about money.

src.t: You’re basically trying to impress people who don’t care about you.
src.zh: 说白了，你一直在努力让那些根本不在乎你的人对你刮目相看。

cards.ex: Who you really are, rather than the person you pretend to be.
exs: Let people see the real you.
Your close friends know the real you.

src.t: And they don’t like the real you, and if they saw the real you, they wouldn’t care.
src.zh: 他们并不喜欢真实的你，就算看到了真实的你，他们也不会在乎。

cards.ex: To miss someone or an opportunity because you do not notice or connect with them.
exs: Don't let good chances pass you by.
Life can pass you by if you only work.

src.t: And the people who would like the real you don’t get to see the real you, so they pass you by.
src.zh: 而那些会喜欢真实的你的人，却看不到真实的你，于是就和你擦肩而过。

cards.note: 文中指“那些本来可能欣赏你的人，因为看不到真实的你而错过与你建立联系”，不是只在路上擦肩。

cards.ex: To admire someone because of their character, actions, or abilities.
exs: I respect her work.
Respect my time, please.

src.t: You only want the respect of the very, very few people that you respect.
src.zh: 你只需要得到极少数你尊重的人的尊重。

cards.ex: To ask for something firmly, as if you have a right to it.
exs: He demanded a refund.
You can't demand respect; you earn it.

src.t: Trying to demand respect from the masses is a fool’s errand.
src.zh: 想强求所有普通大众都尊重你，根本是一件注定徒劳的事。

cards.ex: A large number of ordinary people considered as a group.
exs: This brand isn't for the masses.
He wants to be loved by the masses.

src.t: Trying to demand respect from the masses is a fool’s errand.
src.zh: 想强求所有普通大众都尊重你，根本是一件注定徒劳的事。

cards.ex: A task that is unlikely to succeed, even if you spend a lot of effort on it.
exs: Trying to please everyone is a fool's errand.
Looking for a perfect client is a fool's errand.

src.t: Trying to demand respect from the masses is a fool’s errand.
src.zh: 想强求所有普通大众都尊重你，根本是一件注定徒劳的事。

lg: 跑了一趟注定白跑的腿。

cards.ex: Not being honest or sincere about what you really think or want.
exs: His apology sounded disingenuous.
It would be disingenuous to say I don't care.
lg: 嘴上说一套，心里想的是另一套。

src.t: There’s a difference between being wrong and disingenuous though.
src.zh: 不过，说错了和明知不真诚却故意那样说，是两回事。

cards.ex: A public statement that says something strongly or officially.
exs: The mayor made a proclamation about the holiday.
Don't judge her by one proclamation.
lg: 站在高处，大声向所有人宣布。

src.t: You yourself are going to be consistent with your past proclamations, so if you’re lying to others, you’re going to be lying to yourself.
src.zh: 你自己会努力和过去的表态保持一致，所以如果你对别人撒谎，你也会对自己撒谎。

cards.ex: Acting or thinking in the same way over time, or matching what you said before.
exs: The results should be consistent with what we promised the client.
She is consistent: she practices every day.
lg: 今天和昨天一个样，前后对得上。

src.t: You yourself are going to be consistent with your past proclamations, so if you’re lying to others, you’re going to be lying to yourself.
src.zh: 你自己会努力和过去的表态保持一致，所以如果你对别人撒谎，你也会对自己撒谎。

cards.ex: Unable to leave or escape from a place or situation.
exs: I don't want to get trapped in the same routine every day.
The cat was trapped in the closet.
lg: 像掉进笼子里，门关上了，想出去却出不去。

src.t: And that’s a mistake not just for the listener, it's a mistake for themselves, because then you’re going to get trapped in a hall of mirrors.
src.zh: 而且这不只是误导听众，对说话的人自己也有害，因为他最后会困在一个真假难辨、不断自我欺骗的“镜子迷宫”里。

cards.ex: Saying or showing what you truly think or feel.
exs: Thank you for your sincere advice.
Her smile was warm and sincere.
lg: 嘴上说的和心里想的是同一件事，没有表演。

cards.ex: An audio or video show that people can listen to or watch online.
exs: I listen to an English podcast at work.
She started a podcast about beauty.
lg: 像随身带的电台节目，想什么时候听就什么时候听。

src.t: For example, I did this Joe Rogan podcast, I don’t know, eight or nine years ago, and people will call out like the one thing that didn’t turn out to be correct.
src.zh: 比如，我大概八九年前参加过一期 Joe Rogan 的播客，后来人们就会专门挑出其中那一件最终被证明不正确的事来说。
